prompt: Give the admiral's briefing to the fleet the night before we resolve my Yelp-review dispute. Full Navy cadence.
response:
Fleet, bring it in.

At first light, we do not sail into battle—we sail into process. Our mission is clear: resolve the Yelp-review dispute with discipline, professionalism, and absolute command of the facts.

We will not fire in anger. We will not drift into emotion. We will not chase every provocation across open water. We will hold formation.

First: review the record. Dates, receipts, messages, screenshots—every log entry secured, every claim tied to evidence. No loose lines on deck.

Second: state the objective. Are we seeking removal, correction, clarification, refund, apology, or simply a fair response? A fleet without an objective is just noise on the horizon.

Third: communicate cleanly. Short sentences. Calm tone. No sarcasm. No broadside insults. We answer what is said, not what we imagine was meant.

Fourth: protect the ship. No private information exposed. No threats. No retaliation. We do not win by becoming the very storm we’re navigating.

If Yelp requests documentation, we provide it. If the other party responds, we assess before we answer. If mediation is possible, we take the channel. If the review stands, we decide whether a measured public response serves the mission.

Remember: the world may see only a review. We see a file, a timeline, a standard, and a reputation. Reputations are not defended by volume. They are defended by precision.

Tonight, rest easy. Check the evidence. Draft the response. Sleep on it. At dawn, we proceed with steady hands and clean decks.

Fleet dismissed.
